module.objective: Mampu berbicara tentang kejadian di masa depan, menyatakan simpati, menggunakan future continuous dan future perfect, serta memahami kosakata tentang uang, nilai, pekerjaan, dan kata penghubung 'by'

subModules.title: Reading Mission: The Future of Money and Reported Speech
subModules.grammarFocus: Reported Speech Statements and Future Time Forms

content.summary: Welcome to Unit 10. In this reading mission, you will explore texts about modern money, financial habits, and how people talk about what others said using reported speech statements. You will also review future continuous and future perfect forms to understand how financial trends evolve over time.

linguisticTarget.grammar: Converting direct speech statements into reported speech by shifting verb tenses and pronouns correctly.
linguisticTarget.vocabulary: Essential financial vocabulary including currency, fortune, reward, tip, owe, bargain, qualifications, and employer.
linguisticTarget.readingStrategy: Scanning texts for specific financial details and identifying reporting verbs used by authors.

learningObjectives: Understand the main ideas of short B2 reading passages regarding money and future trends.
Locate specific financial details, numerical figures, and direct quotes within a text.
Recognize and apply correct backshift rules when converting statements into reported speech.

contextWarmup.prompt: Which of these statements best describes how most people will handle money in the next twenty years?
options: People will exclusively use physical paper banknotes and coins for every transaction.
Society will transition almost entirely to digital currency and electronic payments.
Gold and silver will replace all existing national banking systems.
contextWarmup.explanation: Current economic trends and technological shifts indicate that digital currency and electronic transactions are rapidly replacing physical cash globally.

rules: When changing direct speech to reported speech, present simple tenses generally shift back to past simple tenses.
Modal verbs change in reported speech, such as 'will' becoming 'would' and 'can' becoming 'could'.
Time and place expressions also change, such as 'tomorrow' becoming 'the following day' or 'here' becoming 'there'.

commonTrap.explanation: Learners often forget to change the tense of the verb when the reporting verb is in the past tense, writing 'He said he has money' instead of 'He said he had money'.
commonTrap.wrong: She told me that she wants to buy a new smartphone tomorrow.
commonTrap.correct: She told me that she wanted to buy a new smartphone the following day.

paragraphs: Financial experts gathered in London last week to discuss how global spending habits are changing. During the conference, one leading economist stated that cash would soon become completely obsolete in major cities. He explained that most transactions were already digital and predicted that society would embrace a unified electronic currency within twenty years. Many attendees noted that younger generations rarely carried paper banknotes or metal coins.

Another speaker discussed the importance of securing proper qualifications before entering the competitive job market. She mentioned that modern employers valued practical skills just as much as university degrees. Furthermore, she pointed out that workers who mastered financial literacy early in life would avoid unnecessary debt and find it much easier to build a secure financial future for themselves and their families.

subModules.title: Writing Mission: Financial Futures and Reported Statements

content.summary: Master the art of writing about financial future events using the future continuous and future perfect tenses, and learn how to construct accurate reported speech statements regarding money and employment.

blueprintItems.title: Step 1: Future Continuous for Ongoing Actions
blueprintItems.formula: Subject + will + be + verb-ing + time expression
blueprintItems.example: By next month, financial analysts will be tracking global inflation rates closely.

blueprintItems.title: Step 2: Future Perfect for Completed Actions
blueprintItems.formula: Subject + will + have + past participle + by-phrase
blueprintItems.example: The central bank will have lowered interest rates by the end of the fiscal year.

blueprintItems.title: Step 3: Reported Speech Statements Backshift
blueprintItems.formula: Reporting Verb (said/told) + that + backshifted tense clause
blueprintItems.example: The manager stated that the company was increasing employee salaries.

mechanicsRules.rule: Always backshift verb tenses by one step when converting direct statements into reported speech in formal writing.
mechanicsRules.badExample: He said that he earns a high salary last year.
mechanicsRules.goodExample: He said that he had earned a high salary the previous year.
mechanicsRules.why: Direct present or past simple shifts to past simple or past perfect in reported statements.

mechanicsRules.rule: Use the preposition 'by' correctly to indicate deadlines, methods, or agents.
mechanicsRules.badExample: The budget must be approved until Friday.
mechanicsRules.goodExample: The budget must be approved by Friday.
mechanicsRules.why: In English, 'by' indicates a deadline or time limit, whereas 'until' indicates duration up to a point.

mechanicsRules.rule: Capitalize currency names only when they start a sentence or form part of a proper title, but lowercase general currency types.
mechanicsRules.badExample: She exchanged her pounds for Us Dollars.
mechanicsRules.goodExample: She exchanged her pounds for US dollars.
mechanicsRules.why: General currencies like pounds, dollars, and euros are common nouns, while specific acronyms like US dollars follow abbreviation rules.

mechanicsChallenges.faultySentence: the financial director said that our department will get a bonus next month
mechanicsChallenges.targetSentence: The financial director said that our department would get a bonus the following month.
mechanicsChallenges.translation: Direktur keuangan mengatakan bahwa departemen kami akan mendapatkan bonus bulan berikutnya.
mechanicsChallenges.keyRule: Backshift 'will' to 'would' and change 'next month' to 'the following month' in reported speech.

mechanicsChallenges.faultySentence: by next december, the company will achieved its annual revenue target
mechanicsChallenges.targetSentence: By next December, the company will have achieved its annual revenue target.
mechanicsChallenges.translation: Pada bulan Desember mendatang, perusahaan akan telah mencapai target pendapatan tahunannya.
mechanicsChallenges.keyRule: Future perfect requires 'will have' followed by the past participle form of the verb.

mechanicsChallenges.faultySentence: she explained me that she had invested her savings in stocks
mechanicsChallenges.targetSentence: She explained to me that she had invested her savings in stocks.
mechanicsChallenges.translation: Dia menjelaskan kepada saya bahwa dia telah menginvestasikan tabungannya di saham.
mechanicsChallenges.keyRule: The verb 'explain' requires the preposition 'to' before an indirect object.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Change the direct speech statement into a reported speech statement using past tense backshift:
practicumQuestions.promptText: Direct speech: "I earn a good salary at my new job," Mark said.
practicumQuestions.hint: Change 'earn' to the past tense and adjust pronouns.
targetAnswers: Mark said that he earned a good salary at his new job.
Mark stated that he earned a good salary at his new job.
practicumQuestions.explanation: In reported speech, present simple 'earn' backshifts to past simple 'earned', and 'my' changes to 'his'.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Complete the sentence with the correct preposition ('by' or 'until') indicating a deadline:
practicumQuestions.promptText: All tax documents must be submitted ________ Friday afternoon.
practicumQuestions.hint: Use the preposition that indicates a deadline limit.
practicumQuestions.explanation: Use 'by' to indicate a deadline or a point in time by which an action must be completed.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Identify and correct the punctuation and capitalization error in the following reported statement:
practicumQuestions.promptText: sarah told me that she is buying stocks tomorrow
practicumQuestions.hint: Ensure proper capitalization at the beginning and backshift the tense and time word.
targetAnswers: Sarah told me that she was buying stocks the next day.
Sarah told me that she was buying stocks the following day.
practicumQuestions.explanation: Proper nouns require capitalization ('Sarah'), 'is buying' backshifts to 'was buying', and 'tomorrow' changes to 'the next day' or 'the following day'.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Write a complete sentence using the future continuous tense about working hours next week:
practicumQuestions.promptText: Prompt: Write about reviewing financial reports at 9 AM next Monday.
practicumQuestions.hint: Use 'will be reviewing' along with the time marker.
targetAnswers: At 9 AM next Monday, I will be reviewing financial reports.
Next Monday at 9 AM, we will be reviewing financial reports.
practicumQuestions.explanation: The future continuous structure (will + be + verb-ing) describes an action that will be in progress at a specific time in the future.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Convert the direct statement into reported speech:
practicumQuestions.promptText: Direct speech: "We will invest our savings in real estate next year," they explained.
practicumQuestions.hint: Change 'will' to 'would' and 'next year' to 'the following year'.
targetAnswers: They explained that they would invest their savings in real estate the following year.
They explained that they would invest their savings in real estate the next year.
practicumQuestions.explanation: Modal verb 'will' changes to 'would', 'our' changes to 'their', and 'next year' changes to 'the following year'.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Fill in the blank with the correct preposition showing method or agent:
practicumQuestions.promptText: The company increased its profits ________ cutting unnecessary operational costs.
practicumQuestions.hint: Use the preposition that explains how something was achieved.
practicumQuestions.explanation: The preposition 'by' is used to indicate the method or way in which an action is performed.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Fix the grammatical errors in this future perfect sentence:
practicumQuestions.promptText: by next month, he will has paid off all his credit card debt
practicumQuestions.hint: Remember the correct auxiliary verb combination for future perfect.
targetAnswers: By next month, he will have paid off all his credit card debt.
practicumQuestions.explanation: Future perfect always uses 'will have' followed by the past participle ('paid'), never 'will has'.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Write a complete sentence using the future perfect tense about achieving a savings milestone:
practicumQuestions.promptText: Prompt: Saving ten thousand dollars by December.
targetAnswers: By December, I will have saved ten thousand dollars.
She will have saved ten thousand dollars by December.
practicumQuestions.explanation: The future perfect tense (will + have + past participle) expresses an action completed before a specific future time.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Rewrite the direct speech into a reported statement with the past perfect tense:
practicumQuestions.promptText: Direct speech: "I lost my wallet yesterday," James confessed.
practicumQuestions.hint: Change simple past 'lost' to past perfect 'had lost'.
targetAnswers: James confessed that he had lost his wallet the day before.
James confessed that he had lost his wallet the previous day.
practicumQuestions.explanation: Simple past tense in direct speech backshifts to past perfect tense ('had lost') in reported speech.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Construct a sentence using 'by' to show location in a financial district setting:
practicumQuestions.promptText: Prompt: Describe a bank located near a major landmark.
practicumQuestions.hint: Use 'by' to mean near or beside.
targetAnswers: The central bank is located by the main stock exchange.
She works at an investment firm by the central square.
practicumQuestions.explanation: The preposition 'by' can denote proximity or location meaning 'beside' or 'near'.

subModules.title: Speaking Lab: Money and Reported Speech

content.summary: In this speaking lab, you will learn how to accurately report statements about money, finance, and career topics using proper tense backshifting, clear sentence stress, and natural intonation patterns.
content.audioGuidance: Pay close attention to how reporting verbs like said and told are pronounced with neutral schwa sounds, while key financial nouns carry the primary pitch movement.

pillars.name: Sentence Stress in Reported Speech
pillars.target: Stress content words while unstressed function words and reporting pronouns blend smoothly
pillars.explanation: When speaking reported statements, native speakers emphasize the new information and financial terms rather than the introductory phrase such as he told me.

pillars.name: Intonation in Statements
pillars.target: Use falling intonation at the end of reported statements to signal completeness
pillars.explanation: A clear downward pitch movement at the end of your sentence shows your listener that you have finished conveying the reported message.

stressPairs.shiftExplanation: The primary stress remains firmly on the first syllable in the noun currency.
Notice how stress shifts when forming derived words in financial contexts.
The root noun bargain stresses the first syllable, while the agent noun shifts slightly in connected speech.
Suffix changes from -er to -ee move the primary stress to the final syllable.

drills.focus: Reported speech backshifting and currency vocabulary
drills.hint: Blend said that smoothly into sedthat with a short vowel sound.

drills.targetText: She told her employer that she needed better qualifications for the job.

drills.focus: Reporting verb told with object pronoun
drills.hint: Ensure the t in told links cleanly to her.

drills.targetText: They explained that they had found a great bargain by shopping online.

drills.hint: Pronounce by with a strong vowel sound when emphasizing the method.

drills.hint: Keep the diphthong in owed round and clear before moving to a.

The specific qualifications and skills required
How you plan to acquire these qualifications by next year
practicumQuestions.targetSentence: My employer requires top qualifications in finance and strong communication skills.
practicumQuestions.phonetic: /maɪ ɪmˈplɔɪə rɪˈkwaɪəz tɒp ˌkwɒlɪfɪˈkeɪʃənz ɪn ˈfaɪnæns ænd strɒŋ kəˌmjuːnɪˈkeɪʃən skɪlz/
practicumQuestions.explanation: Maintain a steady tempo and use correct stress patterns for professional vocabulary.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Respond naturally to your colleague reporting a conversation about money.
practicumQuestions.audioPrompt: Your colleague says, 'The manager told me that our salaries would increase by next month.' How do you reply in reported speech or response?
practicumQuestions.scenarioContext: You are talking to a colleague at the office about recent financial announcements from management.
practicumQuestions.targetSentence: He told me that our salaries would increase by next month.
practicumQuestions.phonetic: /hiː təʊld miː ðæt ˈsæləriz wʊd ˈɪnkriːs baɪ nɛkst mʌnθ/
practicumQuestions.explanation: Ensure your tone reflects interest and uses appropriate modal backshifting.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Respond to a friend asking about a reported financial debt.
practicumQuestions.audioPrompt: Your friend asks, 'Did John mention how much money he owed you?' How do you respond?
practicumQuestions.scenarioContext: Discussing a missing loan amount with a mutual friend.
practicumQuestions.targetSentence: John said that he owed me fifty dollars for the ticket.
practicumQuestions.phonetic: /dʒɒn sɛd ðæt hiː əʊd miː ˈfɪfti ˈdɒləz fɔː ðə ˈtɪkɪt/
practicumQuestions.explanation: Pronounce reporting verbs clearly with correct past tense forms.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Participate in a roleplay about finding lost items and a reward.
practicumQuestions.audioPrompt: The owner of a lost wallet says, 'I promised a generous reward to anyone who returned it.' How do you reply?
practicumQuestions.scenarioContext: Returning a lost item to its owner in a public place.
practicumQuestions.targetSentence: She explained that she had offered a cash reward for finding her wallet.
practicumQuestions.phonetic: /ʃiː ɪkˈspleɪnd ðæt ʃiː hæd ˈɒfəd ə kæʃ rɪˈwɔːd fɔː ˈfaɪndɪŋ hɜːr ˈwɒlɪt/
practicumQuestions.explanation: Use past perfect backshifting correctly in your spoken response.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Engage in a negotiation dialogue about currency exchange rates.
practicumQuestions.audioPrompt: A bank teller says, 'The foreign currency exchange rate dropped this morning.' How do you report or respond to this?
practicumQuestions.scenarioContext: At a currency exchange counter discussing market changes.
practicumQuestions.targetSentence: The clerk stated that the currency exchange rate had dropped significantly.
practicumQuestions.phonetic: /ðə klɑːk ˈsteɪtɪd ðæt ðə ˈkʌrənsi ɪksˈtʃeɪndʒ reɪt hæd drɒpt sɪɡˈnɪfɪkəntli/
practicumQuestions.explanation: Articulate formal reporting verbs like stated with precise consonant clusters.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Read the target sentence aloud, focusing on the correct pronunciation of financial vocabulary terms.
practicumQuestions.audioPrompt: Say this sentence clearly: 'An employer must provide proper qualifications before paying a high salary.'
practicumQuestions.targetSentence: An employer must provide proper qualifications before paying a high salary.
practicumQuestions.phonetic: /æn ɪmˈplɔɪə mʌst prəˈvaɪd ˈprɒpə ˌkwɒlɪfɪˈkeɪʃənz bɪˈfɔːr ˈpeɪɪŋ ə haɪ ˈsæləri/
practicumQuestions.explanation: Enunciate every syllable of the target vocabulary words without rushing.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Read the reported speech statement aloud, ensuring accurate backshifting of tenses.
practicumQuestions.audioPrompt: Say this sentence clearly: 'He said that he was saving his fortune for a rainy day.'
practicumQuestions.targetSentence: He said that he was saving his fortune for a rainy day.
practicumQuestions.phonetic: /hiː sɛd ðæt hiː wɒz ˈseɪvɪŋ hɪz ˈfɔːtʃuːn fɔːr ə ˈreɪni deɪ/
practicumQuestions.explanation: Practice shifting present continuous into past continuous smoothly after the reporting verb.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Pronounce the multi-syllable words with correct primary stress placement.
practicumQuestions.audioPrompt: Practice stressing the correct syllables in: 'currency, fortune, bargain, employer.'
practicumQuestions.targetSentence: Currency, fortune, bargain, and employer are essential money terms.
practicumQuestions.phonetic: /ˈkʌrənsi, ˈfɔːtʃuːn, ˈbɑːɡɪn, ænd ɪmˈplɔɪə ɑːr ɪˈsɛnʃəl ˈmʌni tɜːmz/
practicumQuestions.explanation: Emphasize the primary stressed syllable while keeping unstressed syllables reduced.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Read the reported statement with a clear falling intonation contour at the end.
practicumQuestions.audioPrompt: Say this sentence with falling intonation: 'She told me that she had found a wonderful bargain.'
practicumQuestions.targetSentence: She told me that she had found a wonderful bargain.
practicumQuestions.phonetic: /ʃiː təʊld miː ðæt ʃiː hæd faʊnd ə ˈwʌndəfəl ˈbɑːɡɪn/
practicumQuestions.explanation: Lower your pitch progressively across the final three words to signal a completed declarative sentence.
